summary: The labels print agmatine sulfate or agmatine at 600 to 1000 mg a serving, with no radiculopathy claim. One trial meets the reading bar: 2670 mg/day for 14 days in herniated lumbar disc radiculopathy, with named primary outcomes favoring agmatine sulfate over placebo (20447305). It is a single short trial, analyzed 61 of 99 randomized, and tested well above what these labels print. Other human studies read are an uncontrolled case series in small fiber neuropathy (32102167), a five-person open-label case series in OCD (41717561), and a combination product in spinal cord injury (42713349). Abstracts only.

population.description: Adults with herniated lumbar disc-associated radiculopathy; 51 randomized to agmatine sulfate and 48 to placebo, 31 and 30 analyzed.

study_contexts.study_design: Open-label dose escalation for safety, followed by a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial

outcomes.name: Average pain measures improved 26.7% of baseline versus 6.0% with placebo (P <= 0.05)
Quality of life scores improved 70.8% of baseline versus 20.0% with placebo (P <= 0.05)

limitations: One trial, one condition, 14 days of treatment.
99 randomized and 61 analyzed; the abstract does not explain the loss of 38 participants.
The abstract lists sensorimotor deficits as a primary measure and gives no result for it.

dose.reported_regimen: Agmatine sulfate 2.670 g/day for 14 days in the randomized phase; the earlier open-label phase escalated 1.335 to 3.560 g/day for 10 to 21 days.

normalization.basis: Assigned daily amount as printed in the source; no conversion.

read_not_used.32102167: Open-label case series, 12 recruited and 11 completed, no control group, painful small fiber neuropathy.
read_not_used.41717561: Open-label case series of five adults with treatment-resistant OCD, added to SSRIs, no control group.
read_not_used.42713349: Fixed combination of inosine monophosphate, agmatine sulphate and L-carnosine; not the ingredient alone.
